source.campaign_title_visible: Have Items to Sell? Turn Your Items Into Cash.

classification.event_product_type: Generic individual-seller acquisition (no event) — same concept as REF-14 with the logo lockup and a blue-accent palette

visual_read.visual_hierarchy: Full logo lockup top-left (large, ~50% width) → 'HAVE ITEMS TO SELL?' uppercase condensed (navy / blue) → blue rule → 'TURN YOUR ITEMS INTO CASH.' → support → four filled blue icon rows → blue CTA 'START YOUR AUCTION TODAY →' → navy step band + 'You Can Do This.' → footer strip.
visual_read.composition_style: As REF-14; the headline is uppercase and the accent colour is the logo's blue rather than red.
visual_read.typography_treatment: Uppercase condensed display headline in navy with the second line in logo blue; sans support; script accents.
visual_read.branding_hierarchy: Official-style logo lockup rendered large at top-left (image-model rendering); band script; no seller.

strongest_attributes: The logo lockup at roughly half the canvas width — the prominence the Owner asked for in 3P.1, shown
Same approved concept as REF-14 with a different type and colour treatment — the Owner approved both, which is variation evidence
Blue drawn from the logo's own 'BID' blue used as the accent
transferable_lessons: Logo lockup at 40–50% of width is inside the Owner's comfort for Advantage.Bid-led creative (3P.1 set 30–40%; widen the ceiling to 50%)
An uppercase display headline is acceptable as a deliberate design choice for a short punchy headline (≤ 4 words per line); title style remains the default
Logo-derived blue is a permitted secondary accent; red remains the attention colour (6 of the 8 new Advantage.Bid-led references use a red CTA)
The same concept may ship in two colour treatments within one campaign
do_not_generalize: The image-model rendering of the logo — production composites the official asset
Blue as the CTA colour by default — the Owner's stated attention colour is red

The collaborator's set repeats a bronze rearing horse, a blue-and-white vase, a stack of books with category-name spines, a gilt landscape, a laptop showing the logo and a handwritten script phrase on a mug/board/box. These are the collaborator's props, not required objects; the engine must not learn them as a checklist.
Uppercase for support lines or labels beyond the headline

use_cases: blue-accent variant of the approved concept

provenance.analysis_method: Direct visual inspection at full resolution; pixel statistics computed from the file; est_* are visual estimates; text transcribed from the image and classified.

logo_treatment_in_reference: Logo lockup in the reference is rendered by the image model (gavel + ADVANTAGE.BID + GET THE ADVANTAGE). Production never reproduces it; it composites brand-assets/logos/advantage-bid-primary.png (or the transparent/white variant) at the prominence rules.
